result.summary:
Independently validated docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-020.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ-020, commit d2e0a9d) against docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md (AC1-AC7), handoffs/WF02-REQ-020/step-02c-security-reviewer.json, and the real implementation (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/start.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts). Read the test-spec file itself in full, not TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary.

What checked out correctly (re-derived myself, not trusted from the spec's own prose):

1. AC1's concurrency case is genuinely a real callback dispatch, not the plain-function test dressed up. Traced the harness: REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN and makeRegisterCallbackHandler are real exports of handlers/registration.ts (confirmed by reading the file: `export const REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN = new RegExp(...)` line 16, `export function makeRegisterCallbackHandler(db)` line 27). The spec's harness registers it via `bot.callbackQuery(REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN, makeRegisterCallbackHandler(db))` on a real `new Bot(...)` instance and dispatches via `bot.handleUpdate(callbackUpdate(...))` -- a real Update object routed through grammY's own matcher, never a hand-called handler function with a fake ctx. `bot.api.config.use()` intercepts only the outbound HTTP layer (captures sendMessage/answerCallbackQuery calls), not the update-dispatch path. Confirmed no mocked/stubbed grammY Context anywhere in the spec -- every dispatch case (AC1-AC9, AC-card) uses this same real-Bot/real-handleUpdate shape, consistent with REQ-013-019's established method. AC1's 30-iteration/4-caller/capacity=3 configuration is genuinely distinct from BACKEND-DEV's (20/2/cap=1) and REVIEWER's (50/2/cap=1, 20/5/cap=2).

2. Catalog strings cross-checked verbatim against apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts's real `registration` block: confirmedPrefix 'You're in!', refusedCancelled 'This event has been cancelled.', refusedFinished 'This event has already finished.', refusedClosed 'Registration for this event is closed.', refusedRequiresInvite 'This event is invite-only.', refusedRequiresApproval 'This event requires organizer approval to register.', waitlistedPrefix 'You're on the waitlist for:', alreadyRegisteredPrefix + statusAdmitted -- all match the spec's quoted text exactly, no invented copy.

3. AC-card's expected `inline_keyboard` shape matches `handlers/start.ts`'s real wiring: `new InlineKeyboard().text(catalog.registration.registerButton, buildRegisterCallbackData(event.id))` produces exactly `[[{text, callback_data}]]`, and `buildRegisterCallbackData`/`REGISTER_CALLBACK_PREFIX` ('register:') in start.ts agree with `REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN` in registration.ts on the exact `register:<eventId>` shape -- confirmed by reading both files, not assumed.

4. Every case states an explicit failure mode ('Pass conditions: ... is a FAIL').

5. AC3's 5000-sample thresholds are statistically sound for uniqueness (birthday-bound collision probability at 256-bit tokens is negligible) and for `distinctHexCharsSeen === 16` (probability a correctly-uniform CSPRNG omits any one of 16 hex digits across 320,000 draws is astronomically below any practical false-failure concern). MINOR concern, not blocking: the `anyPathologicalRun` check (a run of 8+ identical consecutive hex chars) has a small but non-zero true-positive-on-a-correct-implementation rate -- expected occurrence across 5000 tokens is roughly 0.0017 (~0.17% chance of a spurious FAIL on a correct CSPRNG). The spec itself names this ('a well-functioning CSPRNG could theoretically produce one... at a rate far below 5000 samples' expected occurrence') but still lists it as a hard pass/fail condition rather than an informational-only note. This is not severe enough to fail the gate on its own (documented, low-probability, and the spec's own text already flags it), but TEST-DESIGNER should soften it to non-blocking/informational in the rework pass since this task's other item is already sending the spec back.

BLOCKING FAILURE -- AC4's boundary case does not test what it claims to test:

This run's own instructions specifically called out AC4 as: 'checks the EXACT `registration_closes_at` boundary (not a full day past it, unlike the existing DB test)'. Checked the real `isRegistrationOpen` (apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts:717-725): `registrationClosesAt === null -> true; otherwise open only when evaluationTime.getTime() < registrationClosesAt.getTime()` -- a strict less-than, so the exact-equality instant is CLOSED (exclusive boundary). This exact-equality property is ALREADY independently unit-tested at the pure-function level in the pre-existing `apps/bot/src/domain/registration.test.ts` line 68-74 ('row 4: registration closed (evaluationTime at or after registrationClosesAt) is refused', constructed with `registrationClosesAt: evalTime` -- literally the same Date instant passed to both fields).

The spec's own AC4 'boundary' live-dispatch case (docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-020.md lines ~374-410) does NOT reproduce this exact-equality property through the handler. It sets the boundary event's `registration_closes_at` to a fixed PAST literal, `2026-09-01T00:00:00Z`, and relies on the live handler's real `new Date()` call landing 'at-or-before now, whenever TEST-RUNNER actually executes this case (today's date is 2026-09-07 or later per the session clock)'. Given the actual session date is already 2026-09-07, this dispatch will observe `evaluationTime` at minimum 6 days after `registrationClosesAt` -- not 'at the exact boundary' in any meaningful sense, and this gap only grows the later this spec is actually run (it is unpinned, not tied to dispatch time). This is structurally the SAME class of test as the spec's own description of 'the existing DB test' it claims to improve on (`registration.db.test.ts` line 221, `registrationClosesAt` one day before the passed evaluationTime) -- except with a larger, undefined margin, making it LESS precise than the test it was written to supersede, not more. The spec's own reasoning paragraph ('This proves the boundary is exclusive of "now" the same way the unit test's exact-equal fixture proves it algebraically') overstates what a multi-day-stale timestamp comparison actually demonstrates: it re-confirms 'closed well after the deadline produces the closed outcome through the handler', which is a real but different property from 'the exact instant is exclusive', and the spec presents it as satisfying the latter.

This is a genuine coverage gap this run's own instructions asked me to specifically scrutinize, not a nitpick: as written, no case anywhere in this spec (live-dispatch or re-run pointer) actually re-verifies the exact-boundary property through the real handler chain, and the spec does not even instruct TEST-RUNNER to re-run the pre-existing exact-equality unit test (`registration.test.ts`'s 'row 4' case) as part of AC4's evidence -- AC4's 'DB-level property already covered' pointer names only `registration.db.test.ts -t "AC4"` (the pure-function file's exact-boundary case is never cited or re-run anywhere in this spec).

Required fix for TEST-DESIGNER (rework, back to Step 3): AC4 must include either (a) an instruction to re-run `apps/bot/src/domain/registration.test.ts -t "row 4"` (or an equivalent -t filter matching that exact-boundary unit case) and quote its real output as part of AC4's evidence, explicitly acknowledging that the exact-instant property is proven at the pure-function level and citing which test proves it, and/or (b) a live-dispatch case that computes `registration_closes_at` at a tight, controlled margin relative to the actual dispatch instant (e.g., read `Date.now()` immediately before constructing the fixture, set `registration_closes_at` to that instant plus a small fixed delta such as 2 seconds, wait past it with a short controlled delay, then dispatch) rather than a static multi-day-stale literal -- so the live case's margin is bounded and known, not an ever-growing, unpinned gap. Either fix (or both) closes the gap; the current spec does neither, so this run's own AC4 boundary-precision requirement is unmet.

Secondary minor issue (not independently blocking, fold into the same rework pass): soften AC3's `anyPathologicalRun` check from a hard pass/fail condition to an informational-only note, per the ~0.17% spurious-failure rate reasoned above.

Everything else in the spec (AC1, AC2, AC3's core uniqueness/format checks, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC-card, AC-schema, AC-catalog) is precise, judgment-free, grounded in real code, and would fail if violated. No 'TODO' found anywhere in the file. This is a single-issue FAIL, not a wholesale rewrite.

issues.description: AC4's boundary live-dispatch case does not test the exact registration_closes_at boundary as the run's own instructions required and as the spec's own text claims. It uses a static, unpinned, multi-day-stale registration_closes_at literal (2026-09-01T00:00:00Z) compared against the live handler's real new Date() call, which will always be at least several days past the deadline (and growing further past it the later this spec is run) -- not the exact instant. The pre-existing pure-function exact-equality test (apps/bot/src/domain/registration.test.ts's 'row 4', which uses registrationClosesAt === evalTime literally) is never cited or re-run anywhere in this spec's AC4 section. Fix: cite/re-run that exact-boundary unit test as part of AC4's evidence, and/or add a live-dispatch case with a tightly-controlled, bounded margin (e.g. now+2s, then dispatch after a short wait) instead of a static past date.

AC3's anyPathologicalRun check (8+ identical consecutive hex chars) has a non-zero (~0.17% across 5000 samples) chance of failing a correct implementation by pure chance, yet is listed as a hard pass/fail condition rather than informational-only. The spec's own text already names this risk. Fold into the same rework pass: soften to informational/non-blocking.

result.next_action: Rework TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3) -- fix AC4's boundary case per the MAJOR issue above, fold in the MINOR AC3 softening, then re-route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b).
